Sabotage

SAB-uh-tahzh — ends like 'garage'; picture someone quietly wrecking the garage's machinery. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To sabotage to deliberately destroy or hinder something for one's own advantage.

Someone had cut the brake lines in an apparent attempt to sabotage the race car before the final lap.

Worked Example

A jealous coworker secretly deletes a colleague's presentation files the night before a big pitch, hoping the colleague will fail and lose the promotion to him instead.

Deliberately wrecking someone else's work for personal gain is exactly what it means to sabotage something. Unlike 'criticize,' which just means finding fault, sabotage means actively destroying or disabling something.

How Sabotage Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

undermine

undermine: to weaken or damage secretly and gradually

disrupt

disrupt: to interrupt or throw into disorder

wreck

wreck: to destroy or ruin completely

Antonyms

support

support: to help or back something

assist

assist: to help someone accomplish something

How Strong Is It? — hinder → sabotage → destroy

hinder vs. sabotage

hinder vs. sabotage: Hinder is weaker than sabotage — hindering just slows something down, while sabotage means deliberately destroying or disabling it.

destroy vs. sabotage

destroy vs. sabotage: Destroy is stronger than sabotage in scale: sabotage is a deliberate, often hidden act meant to disable something, but destroy means to wipe it out entirely, whether hidden or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sabot-

root — sabot-: wooden shoe (French)

suffix — -age

suffix — -age: action or result of (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Sabotage pairs French sabot, a wooden shoe, with -age, 'action or result of' -- tradition holds the word grew from workers damaging machinery, though historians debate the exact link. Either way, sabotage is literally 'wooden-shoe action': deliberate, disruptive damage.

Use the root in a new word: saboteur

Use the root in a new word: saboteur: The saboteur was caught trying to cut the factory's main power line.
